note: A principal in a currency other than US dollars, converted at the report date (spec 6.4). A dollar principal is not touched; the default rule gd_principal_usd_usd covers it.
A fair value tagged in a foreign unit is taken as dollars (pipeline/monetary_units.py resolve_bdc_units: fair value and cost only, not principal).
A cost tagged in a foreign unit is taken as dollars (same source).
A cost tagged twice, once in US dollars and once in another currency, with two numbers: the dollar fact is the cost (pipeline/cost_in_two_units.py).
Same context, no principal fact: the foreign cost fact is the principal in that currency (pipeline/cost_in_two_units.py).

No principal, a share count on a debt row: the count times a power of a thousand is the principal (pipeline/staging_bdc.py par_scale). Which rows depends on the rule's parameter (row mode or whole filing).
Same rows: the count moves to the principal, so shares is left empty (production sets shares to null).

In a listed filing, an equity row with no share count and a principal fact: the principal is the unit count (pipeline/staging_bdc.py units_from_principal). The principal is kept as filed, as production does.
In a listed filing, a fair value whose printed brackets disagree with its tagged sign takes the printed sign (pipeline/printed_sign.py).

A fund rule naming as_filed acts on share of net assets only: a filing whose pure share of net assets is already a percent (printed 4.0, tagged 4.0) keeps the number instead of the default fraction_to_percent. Slice 3 Task 3 fix round 1.

The interest-rate tag of the filer holds the all-in rate (pipeline/financial_conventions.py prepare, rate_reading all_in). All-in = the tag times 100; cash leg = all-in less the PIK rate where a PIK rate is read, else left empty (production leaves it null). A PIK rate above the rate plus 0.01 leaves both unresolved (pik_above_rate), as production does. A cash-pay tag is the cash leg whatever the reading (production: the concept names its own kind). Production reaches all_in here by an earlier branch where the row has no PIK rate and its text names no PIK (names_pik), and by this reading otherwise; both give all-in = the tag and a null cash leg when no PIK rate is read, so the text does not change the result for this reading.

The interest-rate tag of the filer holds the cash leg (same function, rate_reading cash_leg). Cash leg = the tag times 100; all-in = cash plus the PIK rate where a PIK rate is read. With no PIK rate the all-in rate is left unresolved (cash_leg_without_pik). That is NOT production: an earlier branch of prepare (plain rate tag, no PIK rate, and the row text names no PIK: names_pik) gives kind all_in and all-in = the tag for every fund, whatever its reading, so production would store the tag as the all-in rate and leave the cash leg null. Its result depends on the row text, which this slice does not read; leaving the row unresolved is a choice made for that reason, not a reproduction. No fund of the five declares this reading.

A row with only a PIK tag: the PIK rate is the whole coupon, all-in (same function, pik_is_coupon). unread_input printed_rate_type_and_loan_class (controller ruling 2026-11-23, slice 4 Task 4): production applies it only to a loan (asset_category, from text) and, for a fund with both readings, only where the row prints a fixed coupon and no reference rate; neither is read here, so every row this action would decide is unresolved, reason text_not_read. WARNING: do not clear unread_input without a selector on the loan class and the printed rate type in int_field_rule; without it the 841 wrong rates measured in slice 4 Task 4 return. The cash leg is left empty: the production code on this branch sets it only from a filed rate.
Same rows: under the coupon reading the PIK tag is not a margin, so no spread is set (production keeps basis_spread empty). Listed so that the spread of such a row is text_not_read too.

A row with only a PIK tag: the PIK rate is a margin over a reference rate (same function, margin_from_pik). unread_input printed_rate_type_and_loan_class: production needs a loan row with a printed reference rate (text, not read here); every row is unresolved, reason text_not_read (controller ruling 2026-11-23). The rate is not known: interest_rate stays unresolved, as in production. WARNING: do not clear unread_input without a selector on the loan class and the printed rate type in int_field_rule; without it the 841 wrong rates measured in slice 4 Task 4 return.

Same rows: the spread is the PIK rate times 100 (production publishes basis_spread = pik_rate, label basis_spread:pik_margin). pik_rate keeps the PIK tag. WARNING: do not clear unread_input without a selector on the loan class and the printed rate type in int_field_rule; without it the 841 wrong rates measured in slice 4 Task 4 return.

A row with a spread and a PIK rate: where the printed total margin equals spread plus PIK (and not the spread alone), production stores spread + PIK as the spread (pipeline/bdc_xbrl_html_bridge.py apply_ixbrl_field_status_overlay, basis_spread:cash_plus_pik_margin). unread_input printed_total_margin: the printed margin is text that no model reads yet, so the rule cannot be decided and the spread is unresolved, reason text_not_read (controller ruling, slice 4 Task 3 fix round 1).
